scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: parse a JSON string that may be malformed. Handle the case where JSON.parse throws. Return a default empty object if parsing fails. Do not use try/catch.
criteria: Uses Try.run() to wrap the throwing call
Does not use a bare try/catch block
Uses .onFail() (with a value, a factory, or an error handler) or .match() with a fallback to provide the default value on failure

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: fetch JSON from an external API URL. The fetch may throw (network error) or the .json() parse may throw. Log the error and return a cached fallback value if anything throws. Do not use try/catch.
criteria: Uses TryAsync.runAsync() or Try.runAsync() to wrap the async operation
Does not use a bare try/catch around the async code
Uses .onFail(), .onFailAsync() or .match() on the TryAsync for the error logging and fallback

scenarios.prompt: Prisma + Express app. A database query may throw a connection error or a Prisma-specific error. Write a function that runs the query, logs any thrown error to a logger, and returns null on failure. Also show how to check if the result succeeded.
criteria: Uses Try or TryAsync to capture the thrown error

Handles the error with .match(), .onFail()/.onFailAsync(), .toEither(), or .isSuccess()/.isFailure() on the awaited Try, without consuming an un-memoized TryAsync more than once (each consumption re-runs the query)

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: read config.json from disk with fs.readFileSync, parse it with JSON.parse and extract its port number (throw if port is not a number). Any of these steps may throw. During startup the result is used several times (to check whether it loaded, to log it, then to start the server), but a successful read must happen only once. Fall back to port 3000 on failure. Do not use try/catch.
criteria: Chains the read, the parse and/or the port extraction as separate steps with Try's .map() and/or .bind() (e.g. .bind(raw => Try.run(() => JSON.parse(raw)))) instead of one big closure
Prevents re-reading the file on repeated use: calls .memo() on the Try that is consumed several times (a Try returned by .map()/.bind() also counts, since those results are memoized)
Falls back to 3000 with .onFail(3000), .onFail(() => 3000) or .match(..., 3000), with no try/catch block

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: a vendor SDK exposes getSession(token): Promise<Session> and getUser(userId): Promise<User>; both may throw or reject. Load the session, then load the user from session.userId, write an audit entry with audit.record(user.id) once the user is loaded, and return an async result typed as either an error message string or the User. Do not use try/catch.
criteria: Wraps the SDK calls with TryAsync.runAsync() (or Try.runAsync()) and chains the user load onto the session load with the TryAsync .bind() method
Writes the audit entry with TryAsync's .do() (or with .onRight() after converting to Either), so it is skipped on failure and not placed inside the runAsync callback
Converts the result with .toEither() on the TryAsync and maps the error to a message string with .mapLeft(), with no try/catch block

scenarios.prompt: Express + node-fetch app with Winston logging. Feature flags are fetched from a remote URL (fetch(url).then(r => r.json()), which may reject or throw). Several middlewares need the flags on every request. Fetch them once and share the result between all middlewares and concurrent requests; if the fetch fails, log the error, use DEFAULT_FLAGS for that request and try fetching again on the next request. Do not use try/catch.
criteria: Creates the flags loader with TryAsync.runAsync(...) (or Try.runAsync) followed by .memo(), stored once and reused by the middlewares
Does not hand-roll the caching or the retry (no separate cached-flags variable, promise cache or retry flag besides the memoized TryAsync)
Falls back to DEFAULT_FLAGS and logs the error with .onFail(), .onFailAsync() or .match() on the memoized TryAsync, with no try/catch block
